- [RCTS.1.2.27] **A refused assert** (optional, `rfcs_roundtrip` only) — an
  `assert` step of an `rfcs_roundtrip` fixture's `steps` may carry `refused`,
  the status the runtime must refuse that assert with, as the negative integer
  in a string, as `runtime_error`'s `code` is ([RCTS.1.2.25]). A harness must
  give the runtime the assert, must fail the fixture unless the runtime refuses
  it with that status, and must then go on to the next step. A bounds refusal of
  a host assert is recorded ([RFCS.6.7]), so this is how a fixture holds the
  recording of one to what follows it. An `assert` step without `refused` that
  the runtime refuses fails the fixture.

  A harness must fail a fixture whose `refused` is not a string, one that
  carries `refused` on a step that is not an `assert`, and one of any other
  `expect.kind` that carries `refused` on a step.
